division_reconstructed.note: No source places this household anywhere — the record gives a name and no address, no street and not even a division. So BOTH halves of this band are dealt rather than read: the south division from the reconstruction order book's own household target by division, and the class from the town model's employment distribution, which puts this household under the placement policy's tradesman_dwellings clause. The frame cottages fall on the side streets behind the principal frontages — the back of the same blocks the stores front, which is how a block parcel comes to deal its meanest roof to its worst street. The deal is seeded on this household's own id, so it is the same on every run — and it is the weakest seat this ladder makes: no lot, no roof, no coordinate and no source behind either half of it.

kin.note: THE MIRROR OF THE ROW ON hh_bourassa_jean_baptiste. THE BURIAL ENTRY NAMES THE FATHER, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT IS CLAIMED. Death entry 5 of Father St Cyr's page, Chicago, 2 July 1835: 'On the 2nd of July 1835, I performed the ecclesiastical burial according to the rites of the Catholic Church on the corpse of John Baptist, son of Leon Bourrassa, 28 days old.' Filed as st_cyr_death_05_1 (decedent) and st_cyr_death_05_2 (parent), and the cards minted from those two rows carry their record ids, so no identification is being made by name here. THE CHILD WAS ALIVE ON THE SCENE DATE: 28 days old at a burial on 2 July 1835 puts his birth about 4 June 1835 and his death the day AFTER 1 July 1835, so the father and son of this row are father and son in the scene. WHO THE CHILD WAS IS NOW SETTLED (T-2179): 'John Baptist' is the forename Jean Baptiste standing where a surname was expected, and he is the Jean Baptiste, son of Léon Bourrasso and Marguerite [Laframboise], whom the same priest baptised at St Mary's on 29 June 1835, born 4 June 1835 — 2 July less 28 days. The burial's card is folded onto the baptism's (card_merge_rulings.json, cluster baptist-bourassa, C15), and the father's two cards onto this one (cluster bourassa-bourrassa, C16).

STATED IN THE REGISTER'S OWN WORDS, AND RESOLVED BY BACK-LINK, NOT BY NAME. Le 29 10bre mil huit cent trente quatre, je soussigné ai baptisé Noel Bourassa fils de Léon Bourassa et de Marguerite Laframboise, âgé de deux ans. Parrain et marraine ont été M. Rowe[?] et Thérèse Peltier Laframboise. Both cards were minted from this entry's rows (st_marys_bapt_1834_23_2_father, st_marys_bapt_1834_23_1_child), so no identification is made here. The father term is the entry's: it names the father of the child.

persons.note: THE ST CYR REGISTER OF 1833-1835 NAMES THIS PERSON IN THE PARISH. Read from church_1833_1835. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G2c), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. church_1833_1835 names this person at Chicago by 29 December 1834 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence. No figure is drawn (L1). THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 1 time, as “BOURASSA LEON”, 1836-06-27: 1 lot in the platted town — lot 1 of block 49 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L1BL49CHIOT, as printed), 0.00 acres stated in all, for $1890.00 (ls1001). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $1890.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: BOURASSA LEON matches Leon Bourrassa: the forename names Leon Bourrassa of the 4 people of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. The surname reaches him through a ruled card merge and not off his card: the town held bourassa_lon until data/residents/card_merge_rulings.json folded it onto this person, and the register's spelling is the one that card carried. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('bourrassa_leon:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

sex_basis.note: THE REGISTER STATES IT. St Mary's baptismal register, in the priest's own hand, entry 1834-23 puts 'Léon Bourassa' in the place of the father; entry 1835-04 puts 'Léon Bourrasso' in the place of the father — so this person was male, and that is read off the entry rather than off the name or the roll. A role and a kinship word are statements about the person; no draw stands against them.

What is claimed is that the sources cited on the member below name them at Chicago, and the grade is the owner's ratified ladder applied by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py --build and spent by tools/mint_civic_residents.py, which prints every refusal. docs/LIBERTIES.md L215 carries the liberty and the tension with L213.
